title: Stoker metadata — DLC
description: `games/<gameId>/dlc/<id>.json`: one piece of downloadable content for a game — an expansion, a soundtrack, a cosmetic pack. Not a game: it has no releases, nothing to start and no achievements of its own (the stores keep a DLC's achievements in its game's list). It has what a store sells it as — a name, external ids, a store page, artwork — and which other DLC of the game it needs. Whether a build carries it, and with which files, is the build's `dlc` fix, which names it by id. The pictures are in this file too: a DLC's page is small and rarely changes, and a folder per DLC would scatter one thing across two files.

id.description: The file's name. Minted once, like a game's id, and what `dlc` fixes and requirements refer to it by.

gameId.description: The game it is content for — the folder it is in.

name.description: The name it is sold under, trademark signs removed. The full name ("Example — Soundtrack"), not a bare "Soundtrack" that only makes sense beside its game.

requires.description: Other DLC of the same game this one needs installed beside it — directly; what it needs through them is walked, never listed. Afterbirth+ requires Afterbirth. Neither Steam nor GOG publishes this in a form that can be read, so every entry is somebody's knowledge.

externalIds.description: Its own ids: a Steam DLC has an AppId of its own, a Switch DLC a title id of its own, a Ubisoft DLC the product ids an install that carries it owns; IGDB and the other databases list many DLC as entries of their own.

notes.description: What somebody needs to know about it: that its content ships inside the base game's files, that it only works from a certain release on. Markdown.
